subject: Small difference between factor-scores and group-mean

messages.author: d096edb922462595
messages.subject: Small difference between factor-scores and group-mean
parts:
Hi Phil,

This is more a technicality, but I do observe some difference between the group mean as displayed in coef(mirt_out) and fscores(mirt_out,full.scores=T,scores.only=T) when latent means are freed in the model. The difference is negligible probably (for a two-factor model with appropriate constraints means are 0.360 and 0.231 with fscores () and 0.362 and 0.233 with coef()).

Could you briefly comment on this?

Many thanks,
Tobi

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Small difference between factor-scores and group-mean
parts:
I'm not really sure what you mean. fscores() obtains empirical estimates for each individual, so computing extra statistics on the collection of scores will almost never equal the original latent means and variances. Unless you are referring to something else?

Phil

Thanks a lot Phil, also for the other responses!

Unfortunately, I did not think about the fact that fscores are estimated in an additional step to initial mirt model (I believe in a Bayesian setting all things are estimated truly conjointly). I initially thought I could easily exploit the fact that scores lie on the same metric to do further modelling, but especially variances of the empirical trait scores are quite different than 1, so this complicates things. Is there any way to impose the initial constraint (i.e. N~(0,1) used in the mirt-model fit onto the fscores() calculation of individual latent trait scores?

Many thanks,
Tobi

On Fri, Feb 27, 2015 at 11:24 AM, Tobias Konitzer <tobias....@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks a lot Phil, also for the other responses!

Unfortunately, I did not think about the fact that fscores are estimated in an additional step to initial mirt model (I believe in a Bayesian setting all things are estimated truly conjointly).

Yes, but you'll have the same issue in Bayesian estimation. The posterior variance of the latent trait scores is not equal to the posterior variance term estimated in the model (you could easily verify that with something like MCMCpack).

I initially thought I could easily exploit the fact that scores lie on the same metric to do further modelling, but especially variances of the empirical trait scores are quite different than 1, so this complicates things. Is there any way to impose the initial constraint (i.e. N~(0,1) used in the mirt-model fit onto the fscores() calculation of individual latent trait scores?

You might want to look into plausible value imputations, that seems to be what you are after. I don't suggest using point estimates for the factor scores, but rather draws from the posteriors and averaging over the secondary analyses using Rubin's methodology (see the ?averageMI function). Cheers.

Phil

Many thanks,
Tobi
